record.context_brief: convex level curves of cmc graphs
record.original_question: Suppose Omega is a bounded convex domain in R^2 and u solves the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega with u = 0 on partial Omega. Determine how the convex level curves of u are distributed as a function of H, and if possible extend Wang's example to the case where Omega is unbounded.

Problem 4.2 (3*). Suppose that Omega is a bounded convex domain. Let u be a solution (4.1) for phi = 0 on partial Omega. Give a control of the distribution of the convex level curves in terms of the value H. Extend the Wang's example, if possible, when Omega is not bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $H>0$ be a constant. Consider the constant–mean–curvature Dirichlet problem
$$\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{Du}{\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}}\right) = 2H \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose solution $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline{\Omega})$ describes a graph of constant mean curvature $H$ spanning $\partial\Omega$. It is known that the level sets $\{u = c\}$ need not all be convex (an example due to X.-J. Wang exhibits non-convex level curves at heights related to $1/(4H)$).

(a) Give a quantitative description, in terms of the value $H$ (and geometric data of $\Omega$), of the distribution of those level curves $\{u = c\}$ that are convex: determine the range of heights $c \in [0, \max_{\overline{\Omega}} u]$ for which $\{u = c\}$ is a convex curve, and characterize the threshold(s) at which convexity is lost.

(b) Extend Wang's counterexample (which produces non-convex level curves of a CMC graph over a bounded convex domain) to the setting where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is an unbounded convex domain, or show that no such extension is possible.
artifact.category_tag: Constant mean curvature graphs and level sets
artifact.status_search_result: Wang's counterexample is known: solutions to the CMC Dirichlet problem on bounded convex planar domains can have non-convex level sets, with non-convexity appearing near height $1/(4|H|)$. Subsequent work (e.g., Jost–Ma–Ou and related papers on level curves of CMC graphs over convex domains) studies partial convexity results, but a complete quantitative control of the distribution of convex level curves in terms of $H$, as well as an extension of Wang's example to unbounded convex domains, does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Level curves of constant mean curvature graphs over convex domains
status_evidence.snippet: Studies convexity properties of level curves of CMC graphs over convex planar domains, referencing Wang's counterexample.
status_evidence.claim: The convexity question for level curves of CMC graphs over convex domains has been studied, with Wang's example showing non-convex level curves can occur.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature graphs in a strip of R^2
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs CMC graphs over unbounded (strip) domains in R^2.
status_evidence.claim: The setting of CMC graphs over unbounded convex domains in R^2 has been investigated, but a direct extension of Wang's non-convex level-curve example to the unbounded case is not established.
